_comment: agent 站 pitfalls 英文 · 第 2 批（MCP 分区的补充条目）。与 _pitfalls-a.en.json 合并使用。
_principles: 同第1 批：判断强度与未核验标记必须保留；参数原样。
git: Assuming it is read-only — it can commit and switch branches
Assuming a container deployment can reach the host repo without help — without a mount it cannot read it
Assuming it can push or open PRs — this server only does local operations
memory: Assuming memory lives only in the current session — it is disk-persisted global state
Assuming deletes need approval — they do not, and a mistaken delete affects every later session
Assuming it is a simple key-value store — it is a knowledge-graph structure
playwright: Assuming allowed-origins works as an access allowlist — the official docs state it is not a security boundary and does not guard redirects
Assuming headless mode stays resident — headless closes after an hour idle by default; headed never closes
Driving MCP in a high-throughput coding workload — the official guidance is to use the CLI + SKILLS instead
sequential-thinking: Assuming it makes the model smarter — it only constrains the output structure; the reasoning ability is the model's own
Assuming it remembers earlier thinking — every call must carry its own full context
Assuming more tools is better — this server has exactly one tool, and that is deliberate
time: Assuming the model knows the exact time itself — it needs the system time rather than guessing
Assuming it can schedule tasks — it only queries the time, it does not schedule
github-mcp: Confusing it with the archived MCP-org reference server — that one lives in servers-archived; this is GitHub's own actively maintained product.
Treating lockdown mode as a security boundary — the official docs say it is a best-effort content filter that does not change what the credential can read or write.
Thinking read-only is just a default — it is an enforced filter: write tools are disabled even when explicitly requested via --tools.
